title_original: The Weekend Read: Chuck Lorre’s Memoir, A New Alec Baldwin Trial Doc, Ron Perlman As Hemingway, ‘Street Fighter’s ’90s Vibes & Life Inside A Whale
excerpt_original: The Weekend Read: Inside ‘The Trial Of Alec Baldwin’, Ron Perlman’s Hemingway, Chuck Lorre's Sitcom Lore, 'Street Fighter' & Life Inside A Whale

blocks.text: Chuck Lorre Dishes On His New Memoir ‘Sitcom’ Image Credit: Sonja Flemming/CBS Chuck Lorre is making the rounds to promote Sitcom , his memoir about hatching and EP-ing some of the biggest sitcom successes. The Long Island-born wannabe musician fell into the comedy game and was involved in the creation of The Big Bang Theory , Two and a Half Men , Young Sheldon , Bookie, Dharma & Greg, Mike & Molly, Mom and others. Lorre’s book includes those vanity cards after the closing credits, plus marked-up pilot scripts from Two and a Half Men, The Kominsky Method and The Big Bang Theory . While helping to create stars of the likes of Jim Parsons, Melissa McCarthy, Allison Janney and others who handled sudden fame and riches well, much of the memoir’s propulsive narrative focuses on the difficult stars who used sudden fame to become narcissistic and make life unnecessarily hard for those around them. Read the full interview here.

‘La Bola Negra’ Directors Javier Ambrossi & Javier Calvo Reveal The Secrets Of Their Spanish Epic Image Credit: Getty Images Penélope Cruz had been a muse to Los Javis — the moniker for Spanish filmmakers Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo — for years before they met for lunch to persuade her to play a singer (more a force of nature, really) in La Bola Negra , an electrifying sensation at Cannes that’s now Spain’s entry for best international feature film Oscar . “I saw her in a clip of Jamón Jamón ,” says Ambrossi, referring to Bigas Luna’s 1992 picture, in which Cruz appeared for the first time opposite her now-husband Javier Bardem. “I was young, and I thought, ‘Who is she ?!’” Calvo was similarly enchanted when he saw Cruz in Pedro Almodóvar’s 1999 Oscar winner All About My Mother . “She’s got that material of the stars,” he says. “When you put a camera in front of her, she can do anything, and she doesn’t even realize what she’s doing. There’s a power , there’s a force guiding her, and that’s amazing to see first-hand.” Read the interview with Los Javis here.

blocks.text: How Alec Baldwin Reacted To Rory Kennedy’s New Doc About His ‘Rust’ Trial Image Credit: Ramsay de Give-Pool/Getty Images Mystery still surrounds the fatal shooting on the set of Alec Baldwin ’s Western Rust , an incident that claimed the life of cinematographer Halyna Hutchins. Did the actor pull the trigger on a prop gun as he rehearsed a scene (he denies that), or did the weapon malfunction and misfire? How did a live round get into the revolver and who brought the lethal ammunition to the set? Why were prosecutors in Santa Fe, NM so intent on charging Baldwin with a crime for what many impartial observers — though not all — saw as a tragic accident? The answers to some of those questions are provided in the new documentary The Trial of Alec Baldwin , directed by Rory Kennedy , which opens in Los Angeles on Friday. The film begins by dispelling one false rumor – that Baldwin initiated the project as some sort of attempt to repair his damaged reputation. Text on screen states flatly, “Baldwin was given no editorial control, nor did he provide any financial support or receive any compensation.” Read the full story here.

blocks.text: Ron Perlman’s New Hemingway Biopic Image Credit: Jack Guy Ron Perlman is still a man of action. The indefatigable Hellboy and Sons of Anarchy star, now 76, has half a dozen films in production, and next year is aiming to play Ernest Hemingway in a new biopic set in Cuba and will co-star in the anticipated Sons of Anarchy spinoff Legends . A year on from Deadline announcing the launch of Perlman’s Asylm Studios banner , we caught up with the veteran actor (who made his screen debut almost 50 years ago) and the company’s co-founder Willie Morris about their indie slate and Perlman’s anticipated studio projects. Read the full interview here.

blocks.text: The ‘Street Fighter’ Review Taking a cue from various attempts to breathe cinematic life into the Mortal Kombat franchise, including one earlier this year, another oldie but goodie from the heyday and beloved universe of video game classics is taking a swing at appealing to new generations of fans who weren’t even born when the iconic game Street Fighter first appeared in 1987. In addition to various animated and TV series takes, there have been a couple of big-screen attempts, the most notable in 1994 with Jean-Claude Van Damme’s Street Fighter which was a box office hit. However, the 2009 attempt, Street Fighter: The Legend Of Chun-Li, was a miserable flop. Now with Legendary and the game’s creator Capcom teaming up we have a new and perhaps the most elaborate reboot yet. Whether anyone was asking for it is another question. Read the review here.

On The Set Of ‘Whalefall’ Image Credit: 20th Century Studios Just as Austin Abrams’ Jay Gardiner finds himself in quite the harrowing predicament of getting trapped in a sperm whale’s stomach after a tangle with a squid, the cast, crew and filmmakers of Whalefall also found themselves in the tricky situation of bringing the premise of Daniel Kraus’ novel to the big screen. It could be called an odyssey of sorts in which Jay faces innumerable challenges to make his way home. When Deadline visited set close to wrapping in September 2025 at Radford Studios, director Brian Duffield joked that The Odyssey had just wrapped filming in response to a remark about all the “cool toys” he had for his film. To back up, Jay’s own decision to seek out the remains of his dead father Mitt Gardiner (Josh Brolin), who has committed suicide by drowning in the Pacific Ocean following his diagnosis with mesothelioma, is what really landed him in this scenario. Just as he has to get scrappy and use anything he can find to get out of there, those behind the making of the movie had to be in constant communication about what it would take to carry out such claustrophobic scenes, many of which took place inside an actual whale stomach manufactured by WETA , Studio Art and Technology and more. Read the full story here to see how the director and author used the whale as a Trojan Horse for a much more emotional father-son tale.
